question.problem: For the function $f(x,y)={cos}^{2}⁡(3x-{y}^{2}),$ evaluate $\frac{∂f}{∂y}$ at the point $(0,\sqrt{\pi }).$
question.worked_solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $y,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

First, we use the chain rule: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({cos}^{2}⁡(3x-{y}^{2})) \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x-{y}^{2})\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x-{y}^{2})) \\  & =-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x-{y}^{2})\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x-{y}^{2})\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(3x-{y}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the sum and constant multiple rules for differentiation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂y} & =-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x-{y}^{2})\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x-{y}^{2})\cdot (3x\frac{∂}{∂y}(1)-\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2})) \\  & =-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x-{y}^{2})\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x-{y}^{2})\cdot (3x\cdot 0-2y) \\  & =4y\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x-{y}^{2})\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x-{y}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the partial derivative at the point $(0,\sqrt{\pi }):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂y}{|}_{(0,\sqrt{\pi })} & =4(\sqrt{\pi })\operatorname{cos}⁡(3(0)-{(\sqrt{\pi })}^{2})\operatorname{sin}⁡(3(0)-{(\sqrt{\pi })}^{2}) \\  & =4\sqrt{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\pi )\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\pi ) \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$
